domain: US Army light-infantry small-unit tactics (FM/ATP 3-21.8, FM 7-8) translated to a top-down deterministic sim: 9-man squad = SL + two 4-man fire teams (TL, automatic rifleman, grenadier, rifleman). World units are METERS, terrain cellSize 5 m. Movement stack = A* polyline (path.ts) -> formation bead/wake model (formation.ts) -> local steering (steering.ts) -> per-tick integrator (combat.ts ~600-696) -> task state machine (tasks.ts). Recommendations cover marching formations & intervals, the security halt / hasty 360 (cigar perimeter), and movement through a populated village, each mapped to a concrete function and given exact m/s figures. Verified against the live cohesion harness (mean paceEff 0.35, jitter spike 729 deg/s on survey-9, lenCV up to 0.63).

principles.title: Cigar-perimeter security halt: contiguous near-side arcs, NEVER index-around-the-ring
principles.realityOrCraft: FM/ATP 3-21.8 short halt = cigar-shaped perimeter: each man steps LATERALLY off the route and faces out on the SAME sector he was already scanning while moving; the column's depth becomes the cigar's long axis and the center stays open for passage. Nobody crosses the formation — you occupy the near side of where you already are. Lead team covers the front hemisphere, trail team the rear, SL+attachments in the center. Men take a knee first, then go prone to cover if the halt holds.
principles.currentGap: holdSecurity() in formation.ts:225-240 lays men on a FULL ring by raw member index: a=(i/n)*2pi+0.4, slot=center+R*(cos a,sin a). Member index 0 and index 4 get assigned to opposite sides of the circle, so a man on the east is ordered to walk to the west slot — straight THROUGH the other 8. That is the 'stuck on each other in a 360' bug. There is no bearing-optimal assignment, no near-side bias, no team-contiguous arcs.
principles.change: Rewrite holdSecurity to build the ring from each man's CURRENT bearing from center, not his index. (1) Define the perimeter axis = direction of travel (use task trail tangent, or centroid->lead). (2) Split the 9 into the two fire teams via byTeam(); lead team owns the forward 180 deg arc (axis +/-90), trail team the rear 180 deg, SL+medic/RTO at center (radius ~0.35R, facing the most open/threat sector). (3) Within each team's half-arc, sort its men by their CURRENT bearing and assign them evenly across that half so each takes the slot nearest where he already stands (Hungarian-lite: greedy nearest-bearing match, then de-conflict any two within ~12 deg by nudging apart). (4) faceLock = outward radial of the assigned slot. (5) Settle: take-a-knee = set stance 'crouch' on arrival, and if cover within ~4 m of the slot, snap slot onto it (reuse findCover / coverAt).
principles.params: R short halt / KLE = 12 m; R deliberate (presence, cordon, census) = 20 m (keep current kind==='kle'?14:20 but treat as the cigar half-width). Half-arc width per team = 180 deg, men spaced ~ (180/teamN) deg = ~45 deg apart at n=4. De-conflict threshold 12 deg. Center group radius 0.35*R. Settle stance: 'crouch' on arrival, 'prone' if t.timer indicates a deliberate hold (>120 s). Cover-snap search radius 4 m.
principles.risk: A bad bearing axis (e.g. lead==center) flips front/rear teams. Verify with a headless dump of the 9 assigned bearings + a 'crossing count' metric (pairs whose straight-line slot paths intersect) — target 0 crossings vs the current ~mid-circle crossings. Re-run cohesion.ts; onstation entry should no longer show the men piling. Guard against R clamped into the COP wire (existing clamp to worldSize-4 stays).

principles.title: Fix the spacing scale to the doctrinal '5 and 10' for THIS valley
principles.realityOrCraft: Doctrinal wedge interval is 10 m, reduced 'to the limit of control' in restrictive terrain — in a tight Afghan valley that reduced interval is ~5 m man-to-man (close enough to keep eyes on your team leader through brush/draws). Inter-team / inter-element gap is ~10-15 m with the SQUAD LEADER riding BETWEEN the two teams so he can control both. The practical training shorthand is '5 and 10': ~5 m between men, ~10 m between teams in close country.
principles.currentGap: planFormation() formation.ts:57-61 sets patrol interval = 9 m, then expect*1.3 pushes it to ~12 m and open<0.4 only trims to ~8.6 m. squadSlots() formation.ts:292 sets inter-team gap = max(interval*2.0, 14) ~= 18 m. Both are wider than doctrine for this restrictive ground and read as a strung-out, gappy column on a top-down view — and the wide gap is part of what makes lenCV/the accordion read badly.
principles.change: In planFormation: drop the patrol base from 9 to 7 (tactical 6, traveling 9), so after the open<0.4 *0.72 restrictive multiplier the working interval lands ~5 m in this valley. Keep expect*1.3 but clamp final spacing to [4, 12] not [3.5, 20]. In squadSlots(): change gap to clamp(interval*1.6, 9, 14) so the inter-team gap is ~10-12 m, not 18. Keep the SL slot at 'back: gap' (already centered between teams) and the trail team at gap*1.8 -> retune to gap + interval*1.4 so the whole column is ~2x interval + 2x gap = ~34 m for 9 men, not ~55 m.
principles.params: interval base: crawl 4, concealed 5, tactical 6, patrol 7, traveling 9, rush 11 (was 4/6/8/9/11/13). Final clamp [4,12] m. Inter-team gap = clamp(interval*1.6, 9, 14) m. Trail-team back = gap + interval*1.4. Target total column length ~30-36 m for 9 men in close terrain.
principles.risk: Tighter spacing raises crowding -> more separation-steer activity at chokes (steering.ts SEP_RADIUS 2.4 m). Watch blocked% in cohesion.ts (currently ~1%). If men start grinding at the gate, the gate file (GATE_SPACING 3.2) is unaffected; only the open-formation interval changes. Verify lenCV drops and the column visually tightens via a Playwright screenshot.

principles.title: Limit turn rate — kill the instant-facing snap that reads as robotic dither
principles.realityOrCraft: A walking man slews his torso/weapon at a bounded rate — on the order of 120-180 deg/s max, and far slower at a walk. A real column walks smooth arcs; it never spins a man 700 deg in a second. Heading should ease toward the desired direction, not teleport to it.
principles.currentGap: combat.ts:652 sets u.facing = u.faceLock ?? angle(dir) EVERY tick with NO rate limit, and halt()/faceLock writes (combat.ts:703) are also instant. On survey-9 the cohesion harness measures jitter = 729 deg/s — a flank/rear man whose faceLock sector or whose steered dir flips frame-to-frame snaps his facing the full amount. This is the dominant 'mechanical, not natural' tell.
principles.change: Add a turn-rate clamp in the integrator. Compute desired = faceLock ?? angle(dir); then u.facing = approachAngle(u.facing, desired, MAX_TURN*dt) using shortest signed angular delta. Apply the SAME clamp in halt() (a man who stops still finishes rotating onto his sector smoothly) and wherever faceLock is honored. Also damp the steering oscillation source: in steering.ts the FAN re-picks a heading each tick; add a small hysteresis (prefer last tick's chosen offset by +0.1 score) so it doesn't flip sides of an obstacle frame-to-frame.
principles.params: MAX_TURN_WALK = 180 deg/s (3.14 rad/s) while moving; MAX_TURN_HALT = 120 deg/s when stationary/aiming-to-sector. Combat aim (combat.ts:820, u.facing toward target) may keep a faster snap or use 360 deg/s. Steering FAN hysteresis bonus = +0.1 to the previously chosen offset. Target: cohesion jitter mean < 30 deg/s, no seed > 120 deg/s.
principles.risk: Too-slow a clamp makes men aim laggily in a firefight (felt 'sluggish'). Keep the combat-aim path fast; only clamp march/security facing. Verify jitter in cohesion.ts falls from 110 mean / 729 peak to <30/<120 with no regression in reachT or paceEff.

principles.title: Raise the doctrinal march pace — the squad currently crawls at ~1/3 speed
principles.realityOrCraft: A foot patrol at 'patrol' technique covers ground at ~1.2-1.5 m/s (a steady tactical walk, ~4-5 km/h) over moderate terrain. The squad should read as MOVING with purpose, easing only at chokes and to keep cohesion — not perpetually crawling.
principles.currentGap: cohesion.ts measures mean paceEff 0.35 (centroid speed / NOMINAL 1.5) — the squad averages ~0.52 m/s, a third of doctrine. On seeds survey-7/survey-9/ridge-11 the pace governor isn't even throttling (paceScale 1.00) yet pace is still 0.06-0.41, so the loss is NOT the governor — it's compounded per-tick multipliers in combat.ts:620-642 (moveCostAt, fitness 0.55+0.45*fit, fatigue, overload, leg) stacking BELOW the floor, plus followers chasing wake slots that lag. survey-9 at 0.06 is a near-freeze: the wake/follower logic in driveFollower is stalling the navigator via the lag-based paceScale.
principles.change: (1) In steerSquad pace governor (formation.ts:163-165) the slowZone = spacing*1.8 collapses with the tighter spacing above; recompute against the NEW interval and raise the floor: nav.paceScale = 1 - 0.35*slow (keep min ~0.65). (2) In combat.ts:642, raise the absolute floor from 0.15 to ~0.5 m/s so a fully-laden man on poor ground still walks visibly. (3) Investigate survey-9 specifically: dump per-tick navigator paceScale + rearmost lag; if lag is high with paceScale 1.0 the freeze is a follower stuck off-wake (driveFollower offWake re-path loop) dragging the centroid metric, not the nav — fix by excluding genuinely-rejoining men from the centroid pace read (the lag calc already excludes blockedTimer>6).
principles.params: Per-tick speed floor 0.15 -> 0.5 m/s (combat.ts:642). Governor floor: paceScale min 0.65 (slow coefficient 0.35). Target paceEff mean >= 0.7 (i.e. >~1.05 m/s centroid), paceP10 >= 0.4, with survey-9 specifically recovered off 0.06.
principles.risk: Raising the floor could let a man push through ground he should be slowed by (steep slope) — keep slope/fatigue as relative drags above the floor. The floor is a 'never freeze' guarantee, not a target. Verify paceEff per-seed rises and reachT (currently mostly -1 = never reached in window) starts showing arrivals.

principles.title: Role-correct slotting: AR & grenadier on the flanks, point/slack lead, tail-end Charlie rear security
principles.realityOrCraft: In a fire-team wedge the team leader is at the point of the wedge; the automatic rifleman (SAW) and grenadier are on the two trailing flanks with interlocking fields of fire (AR typically left, grenadier right); the rifleman is the scout/point or slack man. Across the squad: lead team's point man (rifleman) is the eyes, SL rides between teams with medic/RTO, and the trail team's last man is TAIL-END CHARLIE walking backward-glancing rear security. The squad's most casualty-producing weapon (the SAW) covers the most dangerous likely-contact flank.
principles.currentGap: addTeamSlots() formation.ts:312-364 already encodes AUTO-left/grenadier-right and tail-end-Charlie face:'rear' (line 337) for the FILE case — good. But in file (the valley default) AR and grenadier collapse to lat=0 (line 335) so the flank-weapon idea is lost, and there is no slack man (lead rifleman sits just off the navigator's shoulder, line 348-354, which is correct). The bigger gap: the navigator is chosen by scoutScore (formation.ts:619) which can put the AR or a weak man on point; doctrine wants the TEAM LEADER controlling and a RIFLEMAN on point ahead of him.
principles.change: Keep the file collapse but (1) ensure the FIRST rifleman of the lead team is the actual point man (back<0, ahead of the navigator/TL) so the TL controls from just behind his point — adjust squadSlots so lead team = [point rifleman (back -interval*0.6)] -> [TL = navigator] -> [AR] -> [grenadier]. (2) Bias scoutScore so a rifleman/TL is preferred as navigator and AUTO roles are penalized harder (already -0.4; make -0.8). (3) Keep tail-end Charlie; additionally give the SECOND man from rear a 'left'/'right' alternating scan so the rear of the column isn't all facing one way.
principles.params: Point man offset: back = -interval*0.6 (ahead of TL). scoutScore AUTO penalty -0.4 -> -0.8; rifleman/TL bonus +0.3 -> +0.5. Rear security: last man face 'rear', second-to-last alternates 'left'/'right'. Flank-scan men (AR/grenadier) keep face 'left'/'right' even in file so the column scans both flanks despite lat=0.
principles.risk: Putting a rifleman on point changes who eats the first round in an ambush (correct doctrinally, but shifts casualty distribution in the sim's combat model). Verify navigator selection is stable (no flip-flop between two equal-score men frame to frame — sort tiebreak by id, already present). No cohesion-metric regression expected; this is a facing/scan-quality change.

principles.title: Village transit: open the interval, drop weapons low-ready, slow to a deliberate pace (escalation-of-force feel)
principles.realityOrCraft: Moving through/near a populated village in COIN: the squad DISPERSES (don't bunch — one grenade can't get two men), drops to a deliberate/tactical pace, muzzles down to low-ready (not trained on civilians), and treats civilians as neutral until they act — escalation of force is shout/show/shove/warning-shot/shoot, so the default posture toward a nearby civilian is non-threatening. Interval opens slightly for IED/blast dispersion but stays within control on a narrow village lane.
principles.currentGap: expectsContact() formation.ts:700-707 returns true near a hostile village (attitude<0) which opens spacing via expect*1.3 — but a NEUTRAL/friendly village (presence/KLE, the common case) gets no special handling: same interval, same pace, no posture change. civilian.ts only models civilian fear of US fired weapons; there's no friendly-side 'ease pace and lower posture near civilians' behavior, so the squad walks through a bazaar at full march reading as aggressive/robotic. roe/rof is set once at step-off (tasks.ts:61) and never softened in a populated area.
principles.change: (1) In planFormation, detect 'in/near a populated village' (w.nearestVillage(center, ~80 m)) independent of attitude and, when present, set technique pace to tactical-equivalent (slow the governor: multiply nav.paceScale target by ~0.75) and nudge interval UP ~1.2x for blast dispersion but clamp tighter to the lane via the existing freeWidth/widthScale. (2) Add a friendly-side village posture in friendly.ts: when not in contact and a civilian is within ~15 m, force rof to 'hold' (low-ready) and faceLock toward the nearest sector NOT containing the civilian (don't muzzle-sweep him). (3) Treat a panicked civilian crowd as a soft obstacle in steering (separation push) so soldiers flow around people rather than through them.
principles.params: Village detect radius 80 m. Pace in village = 0.75x governor target (~tactical 1.2 m/s feel). Interval *1.2 but clamp to lane width via widthScale. Civilian low-ready trigger: civilian within 15 m & no contact -> rof 'hold'. Separation from civilians: treat as neighbor with SEP_RADIUS ~3 m in steering. EoF: keep roe gate as-is for fires, just change posture/pace.
principles.risk: Forcing rof 'hold' near civilians could blunt legitimate self-defense if an insurgent is mixed into a crowd — gate it on !contact only, so the instant rounds crack the friendlyBrain contact branch (friendly.ts:64) overrides and frees weapons. Verify in the live game (Playwright) that a presence patrol through a friendly village now ambles and low-readies rather than marching muzzle-up; screenshot for the record.

paramTargets: MARCH INTERVALS (close valley terrain, the '5 and 10' rule): man-to-man ~5 m (doctrinal 10 m wedge reduced 'to limit of control'); inter-team / inter-element gap ~10-12 m with SL riding BETWEEN teams; total 9-man column length ~30-36 m. Open ground would be 10 m / 14 m, but this valley files. PACE: patrol 1.5 m/s nominal, deliberate/tactical 1.2 m/s, ease (never freeze) floor 0.5 m/s; target cohesion paceEff >= 0.7. TURN RATE: 180 deg/s moving, 120 deg/s on a security sector, combat-aim up to 360 deg/s; target jitter < 30 deg/s mean, < 120 deg/s worst seed. SECURITY HALT (cigar perimeter): R = 12 m short halt / KLE, 20 m deliberate; lead team forward 180-deg arc, trail team rear 180-deg arc, SL+medic/RTO center at 0.35R; men ~45 deg apart within each half-arc; de-conflict any pair within 12 deg; settle take-a-knee (crouch) on arrival, prone if hold > 120 s; cover-snap within 4 m. VILLAGE: detect 80 m, pace 0.75x, interval 1.2x (clamped to lane), low-ready (rof hold) when a civilian is within 15 m and no contact, civilian separation radius 3 m.
pitfalls: (1) DO NOT assign security-halt slots by member index around a full 2pi ring (current holdSecurity) — it orders men to walk across the formation; this is the #1 'stuck on each other' cause. Assign by each man's CURRENT bearing into a CONTIGUOUS team arc (near-side occupation = cigar perimeter), never the far side. (2) DO NOT set u.facing = desired instantly every tick (current combat.ts:652) — it produces 700+ deg/s snap that reads as robotic dither; clamp the slew. (3) DO NOT widen intervals for 'realism' in this restrictive valley — doctrine says reduce to the limit of control; 18 m inter-team gaps look strung-out top-down and worsen the accordion. (4) DO NOT let the pace governor or stacked per-tick speed multipliers floor the squad at ~0.15 m/s — the squad must always visibly move (>=0.5 m/s); a 'freeze' is never doctrinal, only an ease. (5) DO NOT throttle the whole patrol off ONE wedged/off-wake man (the lag calc already excludes blockedTimer>6 — keep that and also exclude men in the offWake rejoin branch from the centroid pace read). (6) DO NOT muzzle-sweep or full-march through a friendly/neutral village — low-ready and ease the pace, but gate it on !contact so weapons free the instant of a real engagement. (7) Determinism: any new assignment/sort (bearing match, navigator pick) MUST have a stable id-based tiebreak (buildSquad already sorts by canonicalIndex then id — preserve it) so the headless sim stays reproducible across seeds.
